script: Players nobody wanted, but refused to give up! In 2013, a Duke guard named Seth Curry went undrafted, even though his father spent sixteen years in the NBA, and his older brother had just turned into one of the best shooters on the planet. Still, nobody would keep Seth around. But two summers later, he did something on a Vegas court that teams couldn't ignore anymore. Playing for the New Orleans Pelicans in the Las Vegas Summer League, Seth caught fire, dropping thirty points in his opener and twenty-five the next night, before he just kept going. Across his first five games, he averaged twenty-five points and led the whole Summer League in scoring, and he did it while living at the free-throw line and knocking down shots at a great clip. But there was a reason scouts still hesitated to bet on him, and it had nothing to do with those numbers. Because before Vegas, Seth had spent two long years buried in the D-League with the Santa Cruz Warriors and the Erie BayHawks, where he made the D-League All-Star team twice. The NBA only ever handed him ten-day contracts, and he never got much playing time. Then that summer flipped his entire career, because days after his tear, the Sacramento Kings gave him a two-year guaranteed deal, his first real NBA contract. The next year he signed with the Dallas Mavericks and finally became a full-time player. The guy nobody wanted didn't just squeak into the league, and he's still playing today, more than ten years later, sitting among the greatest three-point shooters the NBA has ever seen.
